```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
library(htmltools)
library(sf)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggiraph)
library(tigris)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

if (!requireNamespace("ggiraph", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop(
    "Package 'ggiraph' is required. Install with: install.packages('ggiraph')",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}
```

```{r data prep, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
shp <- st_read("inputs/sections.shp", quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(5070) |>
  arrange(MAP_UNIT_N) |>
  filter(!grepl("water", MAP_UNIT_N, ignore.case = TRUE))

report_files <- list.files(
  "reports",
  pattern = "\\.html$",
  full.names = FALSE
)

reports <- tibble(
  MAP_UNIT_N = report_files |>
    tools::file_path_sans_ext() |>
    (\(x) gsub("_", " ", x))() |>
    trimws(),
  path = file.path("reports", report_files)
)

shp <- shp |>
  left_join(reports, by = "MAP_UNIT_N") |>
  mutate(
    has_report = !is.na(path),
    onclick = ifelse(
      has_report,
      paste0("window.open(\"./", path, "\",\"_blank\");"),
      "alert(\"No report available yet for this section.\");"
    ),
    tooltip = paste0(
      "<b>", MAP_UNIT_N, "</b>",
      ifelse(has_report, "<br><i>Click to open report</i>", "<br><i>No report yet</i>")
    )
  )

states_map <- tigris::states(cb = TRUE, progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  st_as_sf() |>
  st_transform(5070) |>
  st_filter(shp, .predicate = st_intersects)
```

# The Map {orientation="columns" scrolling="false"}

## Column {width=70%}



```{r clickable map, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
map_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = states_map,
    fill = "#424345",
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_sf_interactive(
    data = shp,
    aes(tooltip = tooltip, onclick = onclick),
    fill = "#f0f2f5",
    color = "#f0f2f5",
    linewidth = 0.15,
    alpha = 0.25
  ) +
  coord_sf(crs = 5070, expand = TRUE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f2f5", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f2f5", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )

map_widget <- girafe(
  ggobj = map_plot,
  width_svg = 14,
  height_svg = 9
) |>
  girafe_options(
    opts_zoom(min = 0.5, max = 10),
    opts_toolbar(position = "topright"),
    opts_hover(css = "stroke:#ffffff;stroke-width:2;cursor:pointer;"),
    opts_hover_inv(css = "fill-opacity:0.35;"),
    opts_selection(type = "none"),
    opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE)
  )

map_widget$sizingPolicy$browser$fill <- TRUE
map_widget$sizingPolicy$browser$padding <- 0
map_widget$sizingPolicy$knitr$figure <- FALSE
map_widget$sizingPolicy$knitr$defaultWidth <- "100%"

map_widget
```

## Column {width=30%}

<h3>Ecological Section Assessments for FSC</h3>

This tool has been developed by [The Nature Conservancy's LANDFIRE staff](https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/f37983671094430ebd23035596deccb6) with oversight by the [Forest Stewardship Council US](https://us.fsc.org/) and review by a diverse set of stakeholders. Its purpose is to support FSC US Forest Management certificate holders with assessments related to Criterion 6.5 and Representative Sample Areas (RSA) requirements within the FSC US Forest Stewardship Standard (FSS V2.0).

The Ecological Sections here are from [Cleland et al. (2017)](https://data-usfs.hub.arcgis.com/datasets/usfs::ecological-sections-feature-layer/explore?location=36.958550%2C-95.780300%2C4), and serve as 'landscapes' within Annex G, Representative Sample Areas.  Input ecosystems data for the analyses comes from the [LANDFIRE](https://landfire.gov/) program, and protected status from US Geological Survey's [Protected Areas Database](https://www.usgs.gov/programs/gap-analysis-project/science/pad-us-data-overview). 

**Click the Ecological Section of interest to access custom report.**

# Resources  {orientation="columns" scrolling="false"}

<h2>LANDFIRE Products Used</h2>

* [Biophysical Settings Spatial Data](https://landfire.gov/vegetation/bps): BpS data represents the vegetation that may have been dominant on the landscape prior to European colonization of North America and is based on both the current biophysical environment and an approximation of the historical disturbance regime
* [Reference Conditions Table](https://landfire.gov/vegetation/bps-models): Reference Conditions table is a tool used to describe the historical conditions of ecosystems, including vegetation types, fire regimes, and ecological processes
* [Existing Vegetation Cover (EVC)](https://landfire.gov/vegetation/evc): Existing Vegetation Cover (EVC) - represents the vertically projected percent cover of the live canopy layer for a 30-m cell
* [Existing Vegetation Height (EVH)](https://landfire.gov/vegetation/evh): Existing Vegetation Height (EVH) - represents the average height of the dominant vegetation for a 30-m cell
* [Existing Vegetation Type](https://landfire.gov/vegetation/evt): Existing Vegetation Type (EVT) - represents the current distribution of the terrestrial ecological systems classification, developed by NatureServe for the western hemisphere, through 2016
* [Succession Classes](https://landfire.gov/vegetation/sclass): Succession Class data categorizes current vegetation composition and structure into different successional classes based on the Biophysical Settings model

<h2>Other Inputs</h2>

* [Ecological Sections Data (Cleland et al., 2017)](https://data-usfs.hub.arcgis.com/datasets/usfs::ecological-sections-feature-layer/explore?location=36.958550%2C-95.780300%2C4).  Ecological polygons used in dashboard to stratify the coterminous US for analysys and report generation.
* [US Geological Survey Protected Areas Database](https://www.usgs.gov/programs/gap-analysis-project/science/pad-us-data-overview).  Data used to quantify levels of protection per Existing Ecosystem within each Ecological Section.
